g.text: server/registry-watch.js reads the 200 newest retirements from Verra's public registry (registry.verra.org,
now on the S&P Global Platts platform) every 10 minutes, with the same request and public client headers the
registry's own site sends. Each row is scored with the snapshot's rules: pipeline/build.py writes
web/data/projects.json, the resolved three-signal category and ICVCM status of every project; the category
gives the research share likely real (Probst et al. 2024). A project that is not in the Berkeley VROD snapshot is shown
as "New project" with no estimate. A beneficiary is linked to a company only when its normalized name equals a name
of one of the 94 reviewed groups. The page shows the 12 newest rows and a summary of all 200; it polls the server
every 60 s. Gold Standard is not included live. If the registry changes its interface, the feed shows "Reconnecting"
